analysis.title: GS MORNING: 1) FX Trader Call Takeaways, 2) 2 Mins Read: IMF Takeaways, 3) TMT Q3 Earnings Review and 4) Brazil Election: 5 Key Charts
key_insights: GS FX Strategy (Teresa Alves) views USD through an AI CapEx lens. AI CapEx has raised US asset return prospects versus the rest of the world while pressuring US inflation and rate differentials. Risks to USD are seen as two-sided.
If CapEx growth proves durable and worries fade, that supports USD. If AI expectations fall sharply, JPY is uniquely placed to benefit, and ILS is flagged as an EM tech hedge.
GS prefers EUR as a funder over CHF or CAD and recommends positioning for the downside tail in EUR. Recent vulnerabilities could lead to larger FX moves that pricing cannot reflect ex-ante.

G10 spot trading (Luke Molyneux) is running risk in EURGBP downside, AUD and NOK longs, and USDJPY shorts. EURGBP may be moving into a new lower range as GBP political and fiscal risk premium has eased after Burnham's party conference speech.

A 1.32 handle in GBPUSD is seen as a solid base to build cash longs into year-end if the Budget next week brings a pullback. EURNOK first downside target is 10.35. NOK is the standout given terms of trade.
USDJPY topside is seen as capped by intervention or selling interest. Paths lower are a tech sell-off or more aggressive BOJ hikes, which are possibly the slightly underpriced tail.
FX options (Brian Dunne) says the best implementation for medium-term JPY strength is 2y USDJPY downside in binary format, as the vol market sees supply in 2y-5y expiries.

In CHF, options positioning is cleaner and GS has rolled into long USD versus CHF call spreads expiring in 6m to 1y. Vanilla USD calls look expensive relative to carry, so GS likes 35d vs 10d USDCHF call spreads.

IMF/Bangkok meetings: surprise at how well DM and EM absorbed the energy shock, but scepticism the resilience lasts. Consensus sees inflation risks skewed higher and central banks leaning hawkish, with investors more hawkish on DM policy than GS.

Geopolitics: Middle East re-escalation is a clear, imminent concern. There was little pushback on the GS view that more oil is getting through Hormuz, and no one expects a breakthrough on Russia/Ukraine.

AI and macro: discussion centred on capex-driven inflation, productivity, labour-market politics and AI's role in rates and USD. Real Money clients have a cautious bias to add US duration, but fiscal dynamics, hyperscaler issuance and non-US yields are seen capping any rally. The view on what turns the Fed: 'when US equities break.'

Fiscal: consensus is that France will be forced to adjust by the market, not politics, and absent spread fragmentation raises the bar for ECB/EU intervention. UK sentiment is positive and a credible Budget could extend UK asset outperformance. In Poland, consensus is that too many hikes are priced.

EM remains constructive on anchored inflation, stable FX and credible central banks, but spreads to the US are tight and policy is diverging. India and South Africa are turning hawkish while Mexico stays dovish. Long BRL (FX and rates) is the strongest consensus trade. Key risk is more robust Fed hikes and a stronger USD.

Asia: rare pessimism on China and India. China expectations shifted from a fiscal push to Beijing raising revenue for mild consolidation. India sees AI as a growth headwind and foreign equity positioning remains heavy. Korea is the favourite, with KRW the top Asia long and KRW front-end receivers and flatteners the only Asian rates market clients like.
Consensus is bearish on PHP, IDR and INR and on EM Asia rates broadly, since US yields above 5% exceed most local yields.

Turkey versus Nigeria: Turkey consensus is more cautious and TRY positioning lightened, with the central bank expected to cut anyway. Nigeria's central bank is more willing to let NGN appreciate while guiding rates lower, with reserves on track to be well above USD 60bn by year-end.

South Africa: GS expects rating upgrades from S&P first, then Moody's. A November SARB hike looks unlikely if the Fed holds in October, but a January hike is plausible. ANC losses in Johannesburg and other key areas could strain the Coalition.

TMT Q3 earnings were broadly solid. Meta, SAP, TXN and IBM beat expectations, reinforcing AI-led advertising, cloud migration, analog recovery and enterprise software demand. LRCX, Nokia, BESI and Pearson had respectable numbers but softer guidance or high expectations limited upside. Telia and RELX were steady.

Meta did not raise capex, but did not answer the question on 2027 capex intensity, pushing it to Q4. It also did not address SpaceX's point that power, cooling and electrical infrastructure, rather than chips alone, constrain AI deployment.

Meta Q3 revenue was $64.60bn versus GSe $63.70bn, Visible Alpha Street $63.47bn and guide of $61.0-64.0bn, up 26% YoY. GS reiterates Buy and raises the 12-month price target from $860 to $885. META trades at about 23x / 19x GS 2027/28 GAAP EPS (ex-cash) after hours.

Brazil runoff: implied USDBRL move over the second round is at highs versus past elections, gap risk is over 4%, and 1m skew is much higher than any prior election. The vol and skew combination implies a distribution like GBPUSD over Brexit, a big Lula tail move.

market_movers.rationale: Q3 revenue of $64.60bn beat GSe $63.70bn, up 26% YoY. GS raises the 12-month price target from $860 to $885 on updated operating estimates and sees a positive risk/reward skew despite a 30% re-rating over two months.

sector_views.rationale: Q3 earnings were broadly solid, with beats from Meta, SAP, TXN and IBM on AI-led advertising, cloud migration, analog recovery and enterprise software demand.

earnings_insights: META Q3 reported total revenue $64.60bn versus GSe $63.70bn, Visible Alpha Street $63.47bn and company guide of $61.0-64.0bn, +26% YoY. Family of Apps revenue $64.16bn (+26% YoY), Reality Labs revenue $443mm ((6)% YoY).
META did not raise capex and pushed the 2027 capex intensity answer to Q4 (GS Johnstone, TMT Spec Sales).
META trades at about 23x 2027 and 19x 2028 GS updated GAAP EPS estimates (ex-cash) based on its after-hours price. META is +30% over the last 2 months versus SPCX +1%.
SAP, TXN and IBM beat expectations. LRCX, Nokia, BESI and Pearson produced respectable numbers, but softer guidance or high investor expectations limited upside. Telia and RELX were steady.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Cited as exceeding most local yields in EM Asia, driving consensus bearishness on PHP, IDR, INR and EM Asia rates.
Reserves on track to exceed this level, with the FX backlog to foreigners essentially cleared, supporting NGN appreciation and lower rates.
Implied gap risk around the presidential runoff is double the level reached after the first round.

trade_ideas.rationale: Carry in the forwards makes vanilla USD calls look expensive relative to vol and skew, and CHF options positioning is cleaner.

trade_ideas.description: Short EURGBP, potentially moving into a new lower range
trade_ideas.rationale: EUR downside risks are well known and GBP political and fiscal risk premium has been reduced.

trade_ideas.description: Long GBPUSD cash on pullbacks around the 1.32 handle into year-end
trade_ideas.rationale: A 1.32 handle is a solid base to build cash longs into year-end, around the Budget next week.

trade_ideas.description: Long AUD and NOK, short EURNOK with a first downside target of 10.35
trade_ideas.rationale: Strong public finances, decent carry profiles, and terms of trade back in vogue, with NOK the standout.
Topside is capped by intervention or selling interest, with downside via a tech sell-off or more aggressive BOJ hikes.
trade_ideas.risk: Intervention or selling interest cap the topside, which cuts both ways, and USD strength if AI CapEx proves durable.

trade_ideas.description: Position for downside tail in EUR as the preferred funder, and use ILS as a tech hedge
trade_ideas.rationale: EUR is preferred over CHF or CAD as a funder given asymmetry, and JPY and ILS benefit if AI expectations fall sharply.

trade_ideas.description: Long BRL (FX and rates), KRW long, and KRW front-end receivers and flatteners (client consensus positioning)
trade_ideas.rationale: Long BRL is the strongest consensus trade in the IMF meetings. KRW is the top Asia long, supported by exports, fiscal revenues and repatriation.
